summary.headline: Five-Star Q2 FY27: record disbursements of Rs 2,078 crore (+74% YoY) and PAT of Rs 299 crore, but management flags spread compression ahead.
summary.overview: Disbursements hit a historical high of Rs 2,078 crore, up 39% QoQ and 74% YoY, while AUM reached Rs 14,640 crore (+14% YoY). Collection efficiency improved to 98.2% and 30+ DPD fell to 11.5% from 12.38%, though GNPA was sticky at 3.48%. PAT was Rs 299 crore, including a Rs 19 crore one-time tax benefit (about Rs 281 crore underlying). Management guided to tighter spreads as cost of funds rises, partly offset by a roughly 1% yield hike on incremental loans effective October 2026.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 299 crore (Rs 281 crore excluding Rs 19 crore one-time tax benefit)
about 7.5% in Q2; about 7.35-7.40% for the year

segments.name: Core geographies (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana)
segments.commentary: Together more than 80% of AUM; management reports no drought-like stress and collections holding up. Tamil Nadu collects best, followed by Andhra and Telangana.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Management says collections are improving month-on-month after the state ordinance impact, and disbursements are being pushed more firmly there.

segments.name: Ticket-size mix (disbursements)
segments.commentary: Sub Rs 3 lakh about 26-27%, Rs 3-5 lakh about 51-52%, above Rs 5 lakh the balance. Target steady state is about 25/50/25.

guidance_outlook: Expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of FY27; slippage around 70 bps for the next couple of quarters.
Incremental yields up about 1% from October 2026, but absorbing it across the book will take roughly 24-36 months (about 8 quarters per management on one question).
Incremental cost of borrowings expected 8.70-8.75% in H2 FY27; book cost of funds to exit FY27 about 12-15 bps higher, near 8.90%.
Spread compression expected: about 10-12 bps for H1 and about 10-15 bps by FY27 exit; margin expansion ruled out.
Growth guidance to be comfortably exceeded; any revised guidance likely after Q3. Opex to AUM to fall 50-75 bps over the next couple of years, to 6.75-7%.
October disbursements about Rs 550 crore (muted), with November and December expected to pick up.
capex_capacity: Added 19 branches in Q2 and 75 over the last year, focused on deepening presence in core geographies.
Active loans about 5.1 lakh, up 5% YoY.
Liquidity about Rs 1,300 crore at September 30; unavailed sanctions about Rs 1,100 crore.
Raised incremental debt of Rs 825 crore at an all-in cost of 8.43%; bank borrowings about 69% of total (67% in Q1).
Second tranche of ADB facility still pending, with hedging cost on the higher side.
demand_pricing: Customer rates raised about 1% on incremental disbursements across risk categories, from about 21-23% to about 22.5-23.9%, effective October 2026.
Top-up loans are about 10-15% of disbursements (Rs 200-300 crore per quarter); incremental top-up disbursal about 50% of the outstanding.
Management says yield hikes will not raise defaults, citing that loans above Rs 5 lakh earlier carried the same yield as sub-Rs 3 lakh loans.
Insurance commission impact from the IRDAI circular is nil, as Five-Star passes insurance premiums through without earning commission.
Gold loan overlap: 40-50% of customers have some gold loan; meaningful overlap about 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: How will asset quality move given the rainfall deficit, and any stress signs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no drought stress in core states; collections in October are in line with July and September, with October D1C1 expected near 98%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the repayment rate rising, and what is the behavioural tenure?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayment rises due to adjusting outstanding on internal top-ups (about 1-2% extra repayments); behavioural tenure to move closer to 4 years, from the 36-37% repayment rate.

qa_highlights.question: How much have customer rates been raised, and when does yield bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1% on incremental disbursements; management agreed that yields have bottomed this quarter, but margin expansion is not expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the write-off recovery trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Recoveries take about 18-24 months given no SARFAESI access on loans below Rs 20 lakh; H1 recoveries were about Rs 20 crore and NPA resolutions Rs 35 crore in Q2 (Rs 25 crore in Q1).

qa_highlights.question: How will cost of funds and spread move?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost of borrowing to rise 20-25 bps vs Q2, with book cost up 12-15 bps by FY27 exit; H1 spread hit about 10-12 bps, roughly 8 bps post-tax.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal expenses from the scaled-up legal recovery vertical and CSR spend based on the 3-year average profit.

risks_watch: Rate cycle: a further 25-50 bp repo hike would add to cost of funds beyond the 10-15 bps built in; December policy is a key watch point.
Stage-3 at 3.48%, with Stage-3 rising about 7-8% in absolute terms; management expects a trend-down only in a couple of quarters.
61-90 DPD bucket slippages flat, leaving a sticky stock in the bucket that drives the 70 bps slippage run-rate.
Written-off pool recovery slow (about Rs 300 crore written off in the last 8 quarters vs Rs 150 crore earlier); management has agreed to consider more disclosure.
MFI exposure about 35-40% of customers and no fresh scrub done; a sector relapse would test the collections set-up.
Revised guidance to come only after Q3; new product line still undisclosed, with details promised next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, collections and operating momentum, with repeated use of phrases like 'historical best'. Cautious and specific on spreads, GNPA stickiness and recovery timing, and evasive on specific AUM growth targets.
key_quotes: Our upward trajectory in disbursements continued during the current quarter as well, where we recorded our historical best disbursement of Rs. 2,078 crores, up 39% over previous quarter and 74% year -on-year.
We expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of the year, despite the industry headwinds.
No, margin expansion is not possible , Nischint, because we are already seeing the effect of the repo rate increase on our existing borrowings.
Our book is fixed. So, we will not be able to change the rate on the existing book. Fresh disbursements will come in at 1% higher yields.

adds.what: 19 branches added in Q2 FY27 (75 over the last year), deepening presence in core geographies

growth.why: Management says AUM growth will comfortably exceed earlier guidance, with revised guidance possibly after Q3; backing is partial (record Rs 2,078 crore disbursements, 19 branches added, ~1% yield hike on incremental loans from October 2026), with no quantified capacity or order book, and spread compression of 10-15 bps is guided by FY27 exit.
